How do I get started?

• Create a profile.
• Choose what you want to block or limit.
• Enable Switchly.

Optional: require NFC/QR to disable, so you can’t turn it off too easily in weak moments.
How does Switchly work (in a nutshell)?
Switchly helps you stay focused by blocking apps, websites, and specific in-app areas (like Shorts/Reels). You choose rules per profile, then Switchly enforces them while it is enabled.
What does the tutorial do?
The tutorial reopens the setup walkthrough: permissions, profile basics, and core features (NFC/QR, schedules, limits). It does not delete your data; it only guides you through setup again.
What features does Switchly have?

Core features: app blocking, website blocking, in-app blocking (like Shorts/Reels/Explore), blocked notifications inbox, profiles, schedules, app/website limits, usage stats, QR/barcode/NFC actions, Quick Settings tiles, widgets, launcher shortcuts, and backup/restore.
Why are some settings grayed out?
Because protection is active. If Switchly is enabled/locked (especially with NFC/QR unlock), critical settings are intentionally disabled to prevent bypassing. Unlock/disable first, then edit.
How does NFC work with Switchly?

Switchly reads an NFC tag trigger. You normally write a Switchly action to the tag, then scanning it can perform actions such as enable, disable, toggle, or temporary mode. Pair UID is only needed for read-only/UID-only tags or per-tag limits.
How to use Switchly with NFC (step by step)

1. Open the NFC writer.
2. Choose the Switchly action.
3. Hold the tag to your phone and write it.
4. Scan the written tag to run its action.

Optional: use “Pair UID” only for read-only/UID-only tags or per-tag limits.
How to use Switchly with QR (step by step)

1. Create a QR trigger in Switchly.
2. Print it or keep it on another device/location.
3. Enable QR control/QR unlock if you want QR to be required.
4. Scan this QR code when you need to unlock, toggle, enable, disable, or switch profile.

You can scan with Switchly’s internal scanner or, on supported devices, with an external camera/QR scanner app.
How do I save my data (backup/restore)?
Sign in first, then open Settings → Account/Cloud backup and create a backup. On a new device (or after reset), sign in with the same account and use Restore to load a backup.
How do I delete my account?
Open Settings → Account → Delete account. This removes your Switchly cloud account data. If you also want a clean phone state, run “Delete all Switchly data” in the in-app reset.
In-app blocking (YouTube, Instagram, Snapchat, X) – how it works

In-app blocking uses Accessibility to detect specific screens (e.g., YouTube Shorts/Subscriptions/You, Instagram Reels/Explore, Snapchat Stories/Spotlight, or X tabs) and redirect you out of them while Switchly is active. Enabled sections are blocked immediately. Mixed Home feeds can be less reliable than dedicated tabs, so Shorts detection is treated as best-effort when opened from feed cards. It is more experimental than whole-app blocking because third-party apps can change their UI, labels, or navigation at any time.
Blocked websites – what happens

Website blocking applies to pages opened in supported browsers while Switchly is active. If a domain is blocked, Switchly prevents loading and can show a blocked screen depending on your settings.\nSupported/tested browsers include Chrome, Brave (stable, beta, nightly), Edge, Opera, Samsung Internet, Firefox, Waterfox, Kiwi, Vivaldi, DuckDuckGo, and Ecosia. Support can still vary by browser version and device because URL bars and view IDs change. If website blocking does not work in one browser, try Chrome or Firefox, or block the browser app itself.
Are rules separate per profile?

Yes. App selections, Website rules, In-app rules, limits, and rule modes are stored per profile. Switching profiles switches to that profile’s own Block selected/Allow selected setup, so rules from another profile should not leak into the active one.
What is Block selected vs. Allow selected?

Block selected means the items you select are blocked. Allow selected is the reverse: selected items stay allowed, while other supported items in that list are blocked. This is useful when you want a strict allowlist instead of picking every distracting app, website, or in-app section manually.
Which apps are supported by In-app rules?

Supported In-app rule cards currently include YouTube, Instagram, X, Snapchat, TikTok, and Facebook. Only installed supported apps are shown. YouTube supports Shorts, Subscriptions, You, mini-player, and picture-in-picture. Instagram and X rules are experimental, Snapchat rules are available, and TikTok/Facebook can appear as experimental when installed.
How do Website rules work with Block selected and Allow selected?

Website rules are profile-based. In Block selected mode, the listed enabled domains are blocked. In Allow selected mode, the listed enabled domains are allowed and other detected websites are blocked. Disabled domains stay visible in the list but are ignored by enforcement.
Blocked notifications – what is stored
Blocked notifications are saved only on your device. Tap an entry to see full details such as app, time, reason, title, message, and additional fields (if available).
What are profiles for?

Profiles contain app selections, website rules, in-app rules, limits, schedules, and rule modes, e.g., “Work”, “Study”, or “Sleep”.\nYou can create, rename, duplicate, or delete profiles.\nThe active profile is always shown at the top.
What is “Temporary settings unlock” in NFC write?

Temporary settings unlock writes an NFC action that temporarily unlocks Switchly settings for the selected duration (for example 10 minutes).

After the timer ends, the previous protection state is restored automatically.

To show this action in the NFC writer, enable it in Toggle Options.
Can I write an “Emergency disable” NFC tag?

No — Emergency disable tags were removed to reduce bypass loops. Emergency unlock is now only available from inside the app under Settings → Emergency unlock.
If you want stricter control for NFC tags, enable “Limit temporary NFC tags” in Toggle Options.
That adds per-tag cooldown and daily limits for Temporary disable and Temporary settings unlock tags.
You can set custom limits per UID in Manage Paired Tags. First enable “Enable paired NFC tags” in Toggle Options, then open Manage Paired Tags and tap a tag to edit Daily uses and Cooldown minutes.
What does “Require NFC tag to disable” do?

When enabled, Switchly can only be disabled by scanning a valid NFC tag.

Manual toggle, Quick Settings tile, and certain controls are locked or show warnings.
This acts like a physical “key” to turn off your restriction profile.
What does Emergency unlock do?

Emergency unlock disables all blocking for a short time (e.g., 15 minutes).\nOpen it from Settings → Emergency unlock. It can only be used once per calendar day. After it ends, Switchly automatically resumes blocking.
Why are some settings grayed out or show a toast?

Some settings are intentionally disabled while protection is active. Most common reasons:
• Switchly is currently enabled
• NFC/QR unlock is required
• A temporary timer/lock is active
• A required permission is missing

This anti-bypass behavior is intentional. If you need to edit critical options, unlock/disable first and then try again.
Can Switchly prevent uninstall?

On a normal personal Android device, no app can reliably hard-block its own uninstall in the same way a managed enterprise device can. Switchly therefore uses uninstall friction instead: it can make uninstall-related screens and Switchly-specific system settings harder to access while protection is active, but it does not claim guaranteed uninstall blocking.
How do I open Developer mode?

Open App Info and long press the version row. A normal tap still runs the version/update check.\n\nLong press now unlocks the Developer mode hub — it no longer jumps directly into ADB tools. Developer mode contains ADB/uninstall-protection tools and live logging tools. After it is unlocked, it is also shown under Settings → Help & About → Info until you turn it off again.
What does Switchly device admin do?

Switchly device admin is an optional admin hook for advanced testing and uninstall friction. It can make uninstalling less convenient, but on a normal personal Android device it is not a real enterprise-grade uninstall lock.\n\nStronger managed protection needs Device Owner or Profile Owner setup through Android management/ADB, which is intentionally limited by Android.
Why do the ADB managed-device commands often not work?

Commands such as set-device-owner or set-profile-owner usually only work in specific provisioning scenarios. Device Owner normally requires a freshly reset/freshly provisioned device before adding Google or other accounts.\n\nIf your phone already has accounts, Android will usually reject Device Owner setup. That is expected and is an Android security limitation, not a Switchly bug.
Using NFC + QR together
You can enable both. This means disabling Switchly requires the allowed method(s) you configured. Pick what fits your setup (e.g., NFC at home + QR as backup).
NFC pairing/UID-only mode

UID-only mode is optional for tags that do not contain a written Switchly action. Normal written Switchly NFC action tags work without pairing as long as NFC control is enabled.\nUse paired tags for read-only/UID-only tags or per-tag limits.\nTo remove or rename paired tags, open Settings → Keys & codes → Paired NFC tags. Pairing is done by scanning a tag in the NFC writer and choosing “Pair UID”.
What does “Pair tag (UID only)” do?

“Pair tag (UID only)” does not write anything to the NFC tag.
Instead, Switchly only reads the tag UID and stores it inside the app.

A paired UID-only tag can be used as a global action when the tag has no written Switchly action. Unpaired blank tags are ignored. Written Switchly action tags do not need pairing.
This is useful for read-only tags or if you do not want the tag to contain a readable action.
Which NFC tag types work?

Best compatibility: NTAG213, NTAG215, NTAG216 (NFC Forum Type 2). In general, most writable NDEF-capable tags work. Avoid locked read-only tags for writing. UID-only pairing also works with tags you cannot write to.
Can I use my own NFC tag?

Yes. Use a writable, NDEF-capable NFC tag and open Switchly → NFC tag writer. Choose the action, then hold the tag to your phone until Android confirms the write.

Recommended tags: NTAG213, NTAG215, or NTAG216. NTAG213 is usually enough for simple actions. Use NTAG215/216 if you want longer profile names or extra data.

If the tag is read-only, locked, too small, or cannot store NDEF data, Switchly may not be able to write an action to it. In that case you can use Pair UID instead, but the action is then stored inside Switchly and not on the tag itself.
Why does writing an NFC tag fail?

Common reasons:

• The tag is locked or read-only.
• The tag is too small for the action URI.
• The tag is not NDEF-formatted or not compatible with normal Android NFC writing.
• The phone moved away before the write finished.
• Another app or the system claimed the tag first.

Try holding the tag still on the NFC antenna area, use a blank NTAG213/215/216 tag, or shorten the profile name. If writing is not possible, pair the tag by UID instead.
Which actions can I write to NFC tags?

Switchly can write these action tags:

• Toggle: switchly://toggle
• Enable: switchly://enable
• Disable: switchly://disable
• Temporary enable: switchly://temp_enable?duration=30
• Temporary disable: switchly://temp_disable?duration=15
• Ask duration: switchly://temp_disable?duration=ask
• Profile action: switchly://temp_enable?profile=Work&duration=30

If profile is missing, the action is universal/global. If duration=ask is used, Switchly asks for the duration when the tag is scanned.
Can I create my own NFC, QR or barcode action?

Yes. Switchly writes short readable action URIs so you can also create your own QR codes or barcodes manually.

Recommended format:
• switchly://toggle
• switchly://enable
• switchly://disable
• switchly://temp_enable?duration=30
• switchly://temp_disable?duration=ask
• switchly://temp_enable?profile=Work&duration=30

Parameters:
• duration=minutes or duration=ask
• profile=Profile name is optional. If no profile is set, the action is universal/global.

Also accepted for compatibility:
• Readable legacy: switchly://action?type=temp_enable&duration=30
• Compact alias: switchly://a?t=te&d=30
• Older tags: switchly://switch/… and switchly://profile/…
How do I use barcodes?
Open Manage barcodes, add a barcode by scanning it or entering it manually, then choose the Switchly action it should trigger. Later, scan the same barcode in Switchly to run that action.
How do schedules work?

Schedules let Switchly react automatically when a condition matches.

A schedule has two parts:
• Condition: when it should become active (time, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or location)
• Action: what Switchly should do when that happens

Examples:
• Time schedule: every weekday from 08:00 to 16:00
• Wi-Fi schedule: while connected to your work network
• Bluetooth schedule: when your car device is connected
• Location schedule: when you enter or leave a place

Some actions only trigger once, while others stay in effect for the whole active period and revert when the schedule ends.
What does the schedule “Action” do?

Each schedule action controls what happens when the schedule becomes active:

• Enable: Turns Switchly on when the schedule starts. It stays on until something else changes it.
• Disable: Turns Switchly off when the schedule starts. It stays off until something else changes it.
• Toggle: Flips the current state once when the schedule triggers.
• Enable & Disable: Turns Switchly on while the schedule is active, then turns it off again when the schedule ends.
• Disable & Enable: Turns Switchly off while the schedule is active, then turns it on again when the schedule ends.

Range-style actions are best when you want a schedule to control both start and end. One-shot actions are better when the schedule should only trigger once.
What schedule types can I use?

Switchly supports time schedules (single time/range/date range), Wi-Fi schedules (SSID), Bluetooth schedules (device name), and location schedules (geofence with radius). You can choose actions like Enable, Disable, Toggle, or Enable+Disable depending on your use case.
Why do Wi-Fi schedules need Location permission?

Android treats the Wi-Fi name (SSID) as location-related information. On newer Android versions, apps need location permission to read the current SSID. On Android 13 and newer, some devices also require Nearby Wi-Fi devices for reliable Wi-Fi trigger detection.

Without these permissions, Wi-Fi schedules cannot reliably detect your current network and may not trigger.

Tip: you can pre-enable the needed permissions in Switchly → Permissions before creating the schedule.
Can schedules react to Bluetooth?

Yes. You can trigger actions when a specific Bluetooth device connects or disconnects, depending on the schedule options. On Android 12 and newer, grant the Nearby devices permission first.\n\nTip: you can pre-enable the permission in Switchly → Permissions before creating the schedule.
How do location schedules work?

Location schedules use geofences: you choose a place, a radius, and whether the action should run on enter, on exit, or both.

To work reliably, Switchly needs precise location. If the trigger should also work while the app is not open, background location (“Allow all the time”) is needed on Android 10 and newer. Android can still delay geofence events a little to save battery, so triggers are usually not truly instant.

Tip: you can pre-enable the needed location permission in Switchly → Permissions before creating the schedule.
What are protection controls/control mode?

Protection controls decide which paths are allowed to enable or disable Switchly.

Depending on the selected control mode, Switchly can accept changes from schedules, NFC tags, QR actions, or manual controls like the home toggle button and Quick Settings tile.

This is not just about unlocking. It defines which control channels are trusted at all.
How do app limits work?
If you set a daily limit, Switchly tracks usage time and blocks the app once the limit is reached.
Where can I set a daily limit?
In the app picker, tap the timer/limit icon next to an app, then choose a preset or “Custom”.
How do I remove a limit?
Set the limit to “No limit”. Then the time cap will no longer be enforced.
What does “Overall” mean in usage statistics?

Overall sums all saved usage data since you started using Switchly (based on locally stored daily values). If you cleared app data or restored an older backup, Overall reflects the currently stored state.
Why does Switchly need Accessibility?

Switchly uses an Accessibility service to detect when you open a blocked app (window/app changes). It only reacts to those events to enforce your profiles. No keystrokes are recorded, and Switchly does not store your screen contents.
Where does usage data come from?

Switchly primarily uses its Accessibility service to detect foreground app changes and record usage time. Usage Access may still be used as a fallback or for compatibility on some screens. Switchly statistics focus on blocking activity and limit-related usage, so allowed or temporarily unlocked usage may not always appear and the stats are not a full Digital Wellbeing replacement.
Do I need the overlay permission?

No. Newer versions of Switchly do not require overlay permission. Blocking is handled via Accessibility and a full-screen blocker. If you granted overlay in an older version, you can safely revoke it in system settings.
Why does Switchly sometimes stop working on Xiaomi/Redmi/POCO devices?

On some Xiaomi, Redmi, and POCO devices, MIUI or HyperOS can stop Accessibility or restrict background behavior very aggressively to save battery. This can make blocking or statistics stop even if Android still shows Accessibility as enabled. In some cases the Accessibility toggle stays on in settings, but the service is no longer really running in the background.

Try this:

• Enable Autostart for Switchly
• Set battery mode to No restrictions/Don’t optimize if available
• Lock Switchly in the Recents screen so the system does not clear it as aggressively
• If available, allow background activity for Switchly
• If you use Wi-Fi triggers, allow Location and on Android 13+ also Nearby Wi-Fi devices
• Turn the Accessibility toggle off and on again once

After changing these settings, also open Switchly → Troubleshoot and check whether Accessibility, notifications, usage access, and Wi-Fi-related permissions are all shown as active.
Does Switchly use a lot of battery?

Switchly is event-based: the Accessibility service reacts when apps change, so there is no constant polling. Battery impact is typically low. If you use Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or location schedules, Android may show an ongoing notification because those features require foreground services on many devices.
Battery permission still shows as needed — what should I do?

If Switchly still shows that battery/background permission is needed, open Switchly → Permissions & Reliability and use the Battery Optimization button if your device shows it.

If your device does not show that shortcut, do it manually:

• Open Android Battery Optimization settings
• Search for Switchly
• Open the Switchly entry
• If available, enable Allow background usage
• Set the battery/background mode to Unrestricted

Some devices use different wording such as No restrictions or Don’t optimize. If Unrestricted does not exist on your device, select the highest background access level available.
What data does Switchly collect?

Most Switchly logic runs locally on your device. Blocking rules, profiles, usage counters, internal logs, and blocked notification entries are stored locally unless you explicitly use an optional backup/export feature.\n\nSwitchly does not sell your data and does not need an account for normal blocking.
What exactly does Switchly Premium include?

Switchly Premium unlocks advanced features.

You get:
• More accent colors and a custom color picker
• Custom temporary lock and unlock durations
• Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and location schedules
• Week, month, year, custom range statistics, and detailed drill-down insights
• Advanced automation and deeper usage insights
How do I get Premium?

Open Settings → Premium. There you can view features and unlock Premium.

Play Store build: Premium uses Google Play Billing.
Direct/Firebase build: Premium can use the direct checkout/restore flow or a Switchly Premium code from selected Salt Tag bundles/direct purchases.
Offline build: online purchases are not available; supported Offline builds can unlock with an offline code.

Google Play promo codes must be redeemed through Google Play, not through the Switchly code field.
Something does not work — what should I check first?

Start with the basics:

• Make sure Switchly itself is enabled.
• Check that you are editing/testing the currently active profile.
• Open Switchly → Permissions & Reliability and check Accessibility, Usage Access, notifications, battery/background access, and schedule-related permissions.
• Check Switchly controls: button, tile, QR, barcode, NFC and schedule actions are separate control channels.
• Reproduce the issue once, then send a support report immediately afterwards so the recent logs still show what happened.

For schedule/location issues, also check battery/background settings and whether the phone has location services enabled.
Why is nothing blocked when Switchly is disabled?

The normal Switchly on/off toggle is a full disable. While Switchly is disabled, app and website blocking are not enforced until you enable it again or an allowed schedule/action enables it.\n\nIf you only want a short break, use Temporary Disable instead. Temporary Disable pauses blocking for the chosen time and then enables Switchly again automatically.
Why do location schedules sometimes fire late or not at all?

Location schedules use Android geofences. Android may delay geofence events to save battery, especially when the phone is idle, battery-restricted, freshly rebooted, or has weak GPS/network location.

For best results:

• Allow precise location.
• Allow background location/“Allow all the time” where Android offers it.
• Set Switchly to unrestricted/not optimized battery usage.
• Keep location services enabled.
• Use a radius that is not too small.

Switchly also performs an initial location check when registering geofences, but the actual enter/exit events are still controlled by Android.
Why is the map empty or gray?

If the visual Google Maps picker is gray or empty, your device/network may be unable to reach Google Maps services. This can happen with Private DNS, VPNs, AdGuard, Pi-hole, NextDNS, router DNS filtering, or work/school Wi-Fi.\n\nTry switching Wi-Fi/mobile data, disabling VPN/ad blocking temporarily, or changing Private DNS. You can still use location search, current location, or manual coordinates instead of the map.
What is included in a support report?

A support report includes troubleshooting details such as app version, device/Android version, active profile, permission status, schedule state, recent internal app logs and diagnostic decisions.\n\nIt does not include your messages, passwords, typed text, screenshots, audio, or full screen contents. The report is only shared when you choose to send/copy it.
How can I contact the developer?

Join the community Discord server for feedback and support:

https://discord.gg/PC5zn2NeCg

For direct support, use the support contact shown in the About/Support screen.
Can I donate to support Switchly?

Switchly is already very low-priced. If you still want to support development, you can use Premium as a tip or donate directly via PayPal: https://www.paypal.com/donate/?hosted_button_id=4CMENNDQCXWZY

What should I enable for reliable background access?

For best reliability, open Switchly → Permissions & Reliability and check these items:

• Accessibility enabled
• Usage Access enabled
• Notifications allowed
• Notification access enabled if you use blocked notifications
• Battery usage set to Unrestricted/Not optimized where available
• Auto-start allowed on aggressive manufacturers
• Exact alarms allowed on Android 12+ if schedules are used
• Location set to precise + “Allow all the time” if Wi-Fi/location schedules are used

The exact names differ by Android version and manufacturer.
Where can I find device-specific background steps?

Some manufacturers aggressively stop apps in the background. A good external checklist is:

https://dontkillmyapp.com/

Open your manufacturer there and apply the relevant Battery/Background activity/Auto-start steps for Switchly. The wording can differ by Android version, but the goal is the same: Switchly should not be optimized, restricted, or prevented from starting in the background.
Why does Switchly show an Android “allow in background” popup?

On supported Android versions, Switchly can ask Android to exclude it from battery optimization. If Android shows the popup and you allow it, Switchly should move closer to Unrestricted/Not optimized battery behavior.\n\nSome devices ignore this popup, hide it, or still require extra OEM settings afterwards. If schedules or blocking feel delayed, also check the Background access guide and your manufacturer steps.
